newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian bonds firm with foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian bonds firm with foreign markets.

text.p: Norwegian bond yields fell with German bunds but the spread initially widened by a few basis points despite favourable figures on economic indicators presented by the national statistics office.
"We were lagging behind the German market," a broker said. "When markets move abroad there is a delayed effect in Norway."
Another broker said: "The market in general has been moving sideways today, but there were some sellers in the two-year segment after the figures from the statistics office were announced".

Statistics Norway, the government department, in a new forecast kept unchanged at 3.1 percent its official projection for oil-rich Norway's overall GDP in 1997. It upgraded estimates for 1998 GDP to 4.2 percent from three percent in a February report.

The bureau forecast CPI growth in 1997 at 2.4 percent, up from 1.8 percent in February. The previous forecast came as the petrocurrency was going through a period of appreciation, but it has since weakened.

The bureau's national account figures for first-quarter overall GDP -- a rise of 0.5 percent year-on-year and a fall of 0.1 percent from the fourth quarter 1996 -- took the market by surprise, according to analysts.
"The first quarter was surprisingly low but some of this may be attributed to a run-down in inventories," said Jon Eriksen at London-based I.D.E.A.

"The new forecast should be reassuring to the market because the statistics office does not see any signs of the economy overheating. Private consumption seems surprisingly well-behaved despite lower interest rates and rising income," he said.
The next domestic factor to watch for the market is Statistics Norway's CPI figures for May on Tuesday.
